name: surprises-1
statement: The Olmo-3.1 RL-Zero-Math gain is two separable components: a domain-general 'enter deliberative mode' shift that the opening cue reproduces exactly and that Code-RL and the 3.0 RL release also learned, plus a termination-calibration component that only 3.1 learned from training truncated rollouts as negatives (stop when the answer is checked, keep checking when it is not, finish before the cap); the ~11-point cued-base gap is the second component alone.
scope: Olmo-3-1025-7B base, Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math, Olmo-3-7B-RL-Zero-Math (3.0), Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Code; MATH-500 and the 328 harder problems, T 0.6 and T 1.0, cap 16,384, grader v3. Does not cover which weights carry each component, the Code benchmarks, or the plain base's temperature loss on short problems.

explains.quote: the cue already equals RL on MATH-500
explains.how: The 3.0 RL release has only the deliberative-mode component, which the cue reproduces, so cue = RL on that pair.

explains.quote: by not masking truncated sequences (they are trained as negatives)
explains.how: This training difference is the source of the termination-calibration component that only 3.1 has, hence the 10.6-point gap exists only against 3.1.
RL already contains the cue's component, so adding the cue to RL changes nothing (a control as good as the treatment).
The cue token appears in late-MLP readouts of both RL deltas but not the imitation delta: the cue-like component is generic to RL-Zero, not math-specific.

explains.quote: D follows the answer format, not correctness
explains.how: The refuted 'RL refuses the quick wrong start' hypothesis fails because RL's change is not at answer starts but in how answers end and are formatted.

explains.quote: RL's P(stop) is below 0.5 in 16.5 % of 473 answers
explains.how: RL declines to stop where the base stops (4.2 %), the signature of a changed termination decision.
RL never commits a short wrong answer, while the base commits 13 wrong of 263 short answers: RL's stop is calibrated to checked answers.
A quarter of the RL-only problems are base runs that never terminate without looping: missing termination, not missing knowledge.

explains.quote: T1 cap hits exceed T2's by 15.2 points in Q4
explains.how: The gap concentrates where finishing within the budget matters, the long problems.
At equal mean tokens, RL has 20 cap hits vs the cued base's 77: RL's length distribution has lost the non-terminating tail that truncation-as-negative training penalises.

explains.quote: the +3.4 difference lies entirely in cap-hit problems
explains.how: The part of the RL delta beyond the generic component acts on termination (cap-hit problems).

explains.quote: from RL's prefix 48 / 41 / 21; from its own prefix 23 / 16 / 38
explains.how: The base can finish from a prefix that RL has steered toward termination, so the base has the math but lacks the ending policy.
A calibrated stop rule makes RL robust to sampling noise, whereas the cued base's endings depend on temperature.

conflicts.how: On the shortest quartile cap hits barely differ, yet the gap is 11 points; termination calibration must explain it through early wrong commits, which is weaker evidence.
Part of the RL-only set looks like skill errors, not termination errors, unless a calibrated re-check catches them.
The Math-RL and Code-RL deltas share little norm, so a shared generic component must be small in norm and large in effect, which is not shown.

rival: RL taught math-specific skill (fewer misreads and slips) beyond what the cue unlocks. It predicts the 3.0 RL release is also well above the cued base on our harness and that Code-RL gives no MATH-500 gain; this theory predicts 3.0 RL equals the cued base with many cap hits and that Code-RL lifts the plain base most of the way to the cued base.

predictions.experiment: allenai/Olmo-3-7B-RL-Zero-Math (3.0 release), plain prompt, MATH-500 n=500, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384, grader v3, one sample
predictions.refuted_by: 3.0 RL scores 450 or more, or has fewer than 10 cap hits (it would then have the termination component too)

predictions.experiment: allenai/Olmo-3-7B-RL-Zero-Math (3.0 release), plain prompt, 328 harder problems, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384, grader v3, one sample
predictions.refuted_by: 3.0 RL scores 195 or more, or has fewer than 40 cap hits

predictions.experiment: Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Code (final checkpoint, = base + Code-RL delta), plain prompt (no cue), MATH-500 n=500, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384, grader v3
predictions.refuted_by: 260 or fewer right (no transfer of the cue-like component over the plain base's 224), or 440 or more (Code-RL would then carry the termination component too)

predictions.experiment: Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Code with the opening cue, MATH-500 n=500, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384, grader v3
predictions.refuted_by: 440 or more: the cue and Code-RL would then add, i.e. they are not the same component

predictions.experiment: Base + cue, MATH-500 n=500, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap raised to 32,768, grader v3, one sample
predictions.refuted_by: 430 or more: the gap would then be token budget, not a missing termination policy
